report.summary: ProvenanceCheck module: verifies candidate's interpreter resolves daedalus inside candidate tree; fail-closed for probe failures.
risks: PROBE_SOURCE | medium | Probe source uses getattr(daedalus,'__file__',None) which may fail silently if daedalus is a namespace package without __file__; __path__ fallback mitigates but not if __path__ empty | Test with namespace package

check_import_provenance | low | timeout_s default 60.0 may be too high for fast probe; subprocess timeout raises TimeoutExpired caught by except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError) but TimeoutExpired is a subclass of SubprocessError, so caught correctly | Confirm exception hierarchy

check_import_provenance | low | raw.get('daedalus_file') can be None for namespace packages; candidates list includes resolved (None) which _under(None, base) returns False; relies on daedalus_path fallback | Ensure __path__ is set for namespace packages

claims.text: the evolution runner called a bare ``pytest``, which put only each test file's own basedir on ``sys.path``.
claims.why: Describes historical behavior; no code in this chunk implements that runner.

claims.text: the runner now uses ``sys.executable -m pytest`` with ``cwd`` set to the worktree, which puts the worktree on ``sys.path[0]``, ahead of ``PathFinder``, ahead of ``_EditableFinder``.
claims.why: Refers to runner implementation not present in this chunk.

claims.text: the candidate wins by an argument about import ordering, and nothing checks the argument still holds.
claims.why: Describes motivation; no code in this chunk checks import ordering argument.

claims.text: It stops holding if: * ``PYTHONPATH`` is set in the environment the evaluator inherits; * a candidate worktree has no ``daedalus/`` directory at all (a partial or destroyed candidate); * a future refactor changes how the editable install registers itself; * somebody "simplifies" the invocation back to bare ``pytest``.
claims.why: Describes scenarios not verifiable from this chunk; module's check_import_provenance does not test these scenarios explicitly.

claims.text: Cheap: one interpreter start, ~0.3 s, against a suite run of seconds to minutes.
claims.why: Performance claim not verifiable from code alone.

claims.text: Run in the CANDIDATE's interpreter, cwd and environment -- not here.
claims.why: check_import_provenance runs subprocess with [exe, '-c', PROBE_SOURCE] and cwd=str(base), using candidate's interpreter and environment.

claims.text: Reporting what ``daedalus`` resolves to in *this* process would answer a different question than the one that matters, and answer it reassuringly.
claims.why: Philosophical claim; no code in this chunk runs in 'this' process to compare.

claims.text: Reports rather than asserts, so the caller decides.
claims.why: check_import_provenance returns ProvenanceCheck object; caller decides how to handle.

claims.text: A probe that exited non-zero on mismatch would be indistinguishable from a probe that failed to start, which is the distinction this whole module is about.
claims.why: Describes design rationale; code does not implement such a probe.

claims.text: Deliberately says "evaluation" and never "candidate": the candidate has not been judged, and a reader must not be able to mistake this for a bad score.
claims.why: as_error returns string starting with 'EVALUATION VOID (not a candidate failure)'.
Function returns ok=False for subprocess failure, non-zero return, unparseable output, import error, or resolution outside tree.

claims.text: A probe that will not start, times out, returns unparseable output, or cannot import ``daedalus`` at all reports ``ok=False``
claims.why: Code returns ProvenanceCheck(False,...) for OSError/SubprocessError, non-zero return, unparseable output, and import_error.

claims.text: because "we could not establish which tree would be scored" and "the wrong tree would be scored" have the same consequence for a promotion decision, and neither is a green light.
claims.why: Design rationale; not verifiable from code.

claims.text: __path__ is checked too: a namespace package has no __file__, and a candidate whose package dir lost its __init__.py would otherwise resolve to None and be read as "no answer" rather than "wrong tree".
claims.why: Code includes candidates = [resolved, *(raw.get('daedalus_path') or [])] and checks any under base.

observations.what: PROBE_SOURCE uses getattr(daedalus,'__file__',None) and daedalus.__path__; if daedalus is a namespace package with __path__ set, __file__ may be None but __path__ should be populated; fallback works.

check_import_provenance returns ok=True if any candidate path is under base; but if daedalus is a namespace package with __path__ containing multiple entries, only one need be under base; others outside are ignored.
The 'resolved' field in ProvenanceCheck is daedalus_file (__file__), which may be None for namespace packages; as_error uses resolved in message, potentially showing 'None'.
